title: We Vetted 2000 AI Skills Before They Reached Developers — Lucas Palma, Nubank
talk_summary: Nubank built 'Skill Vector', a CI gate that scans AI skills/plugins/MCP servers before they reach an internal marketplace, combining deterministic regex checks with LLM review and posting findings as PR comments plus SARIF for vulnerability management. They scanned 2000+ skills, found 1500+ risks, remediated ~1000 and blocked a few malicious ones.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid deterministic + LLM scan gate on agent artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: Run cheap regex/deterministic checks first for known-bad patterns (destructive shell, hardcoded credentials, over-broad permissions), then escalate to LLM review only for behavior/context judgment, because LLM verdicts vary with temperature.
takeaways.numbers: 2000+ skills scanned, 1500+ risks found, ~1000 remediated, a few blocked

takeaways.technique: Findings posted as PR comments + SARIF feed
takeaways.what_they_do: Scanner output is written back into the same PR the engineer opened, and also emitted as SARIF consumed by security tooling and the vulnerability management program, with severity/policy deciding allow / remediate / block.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of these findings are reporting the PR that was open to upload the skill ... to have a serif with all of these so it can be consumed by our security tools

takeaways.technique: Same scanner runnable locally and enforced in CI
takeaways.what_they_do: Engineers can run the scan locally and iterate until clean before upload; CI re-runs the identical checks after upload so a stale or skipped local run can't slip through.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the engineers are able to use it locally and also be iterating until the skill is being considered safe before uploaded it and after them upload the skill. We also runs it again

takeaways.what_they_do: They scan for prompts that say 'ask for confirmation' where the agent can confirm to itself, and check that approvals actually route through real approval gates/hooks rather than model self-approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the AI may ask confirmation for itself. So from your perspective there is a human in the loop but for the AI perspective there is has been a confirmation

takeaways.technique: Treat skills/plugins/MCP/rules as supply chain with per-type gates
takeaways.what_they_do: Same vetting pipeline extended to plugins, MCP servers, agent rules and hooks, each with its own risk model and policy-driven gates; third-party downloads must be re-uploaded to the canonical marketplace to be scanned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of these as I said could be applied to plugins to MCP servers rules hooks ... having also different gates depending on policies

takeaways.technique: Historical back-scan to find latent risks
takeaways.what_they_do: After building the scanner they re-ran it over all previously created skills to surface risks that predated the gate, feeding them into vulnerability management for remediation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also had made a b uh historical scan looking upon the skills that were created before the skill v implemented ... we were able to identify new uh risks
